inline-validation.name: Inline Validation
inline-validation.purpose: Provide visible field-level validation, confirmation, or guidance tied to the field that owns the issue.
inline-validation.statePrecedence: disabled > error > warning > success > info > default

Energy.decision: Use Energy for severity color and readable field border.
Energy.behavior: Severity is visible with text and icon.

Voice.decision: Use Voice for concise recovery copy.

Frame.decision: Use Frame for spacing, width, and field-message relationship.

Depth.decision: Use Depth only through parent form surfaces.

Momentum.decision: Use Momentum for subtle state changes and reduced motion.
Momentum.behavior: State changes do not distract typing.

State.decision: Use State for default, info, success, warning, error, and disabled.

Tone.decision: Use Tone for calm, precise recovery language.

Growth.decision: Use Growth to escalate group/page issues to patterns.

Symbol.decision: Use Symbol for optional severity icons.

Iconography.decision: Use Iconography for message icon alignment.

Accessibility.decision: Use Accessibility for aria-describedby, aria-invalid, and announcement timing.
Accessibility.behavior: Field and message are programmatically connected.

dont: Do not hide in Tooltip or Toast.
Do not use for global issues.
Do not rely on color alone.
info: Group or page issues should escalate to patterns.

agentInstructions: Use Inline Validation only for field-owned feedback.
Ask when the issue belongs to a group or page.
Connect field and message ids; do not render a duplicate field when an owning field already exists.
Use live only when validation appears after user action.

props.name: id
props.notes: Stable field id used to wire aria-describedby.

props.name: fullWidth
props.notes: Lets the validation field and message fill the owning field column.

props.name: field
props.notes: Controls whether the component renders a field preview or only the attached validation message.

props.name: live
props.notes: Announces dynamic validation after user action; errors use alert, non-error states use status.
